title: Off BroadStreet presents: SHA-LA-LA
description: Starring Tina Marie Kelley, Artemis Arthur, Emily Fitzpatrick & Lindsay Grimes!, In 1984, a wealthy Fresno socialite, a psychologist, a Broadway actress and a high school choir teacher all have one thing in common: while in college in the 1960's, they performed as a vocal quartet known as Sha-La-La. Now, years after going their separate ways, in order to fulfill a fourteen- year-old promise, they must return to their Alma Mater and present a stunning performance of memorable 1960's, ‘70's and ‘80's hits. These lovable ladies will take you on a wonderful, hilarious, uplifting and nostalgic trip through three decades of America’s best music! , Doors open at 6 pm (Fri + Sat) - w/ Musical performances by local acts, Show starts at 7:15 pm, For Sunday Matinee, Doors open at 1 pm Show starts at 2 pm

title: Flameworking Everything Marbles
description: Small spheres. Big satisfaction., Are the kids still playing marbles and jacks? Maybe… maybe not—but in this class, marbles take center stage. Everything Marbles! is a playful, hands-on lampworking workshop where participants of all ages and experience levels learn the fundamentals of making beautiful, handmade glass marbles on the torch., This class is all about building strong foundations while having fun. You’ll explore how molten glass gathers, moves, and responds to heat and gravity as you shape, color, and finish your own unique marbles. Along the way, we’ll also demystify the annealing process and why it’s essential to creating strong, finished glass pieces., Whether you’re brand new to lampworking or looking to expand your skills, this class offers a welcoming entry point into torchwork—and a great way to start (or grow) a marble collection made entirely by you., What You’ll CreateClear glass marbles, Outside-color marbles, Inside-color marbles, What You’ll LearnBasic heat control on the torch, Gathering and shaping molten glass, Applying color inside and outside the marble, Gravity and marvering techniques, How to use a marble mold, An introduction to annealing and the cooling process, Class DetailsSkill Level: All levels welcome (no prior experience required), Format: One hands-on workshop, Ages: Adults & Teens 12 +, Class Size: Small-group instruction for personalized guidance, Materials: All glass and tools provided, Please wear natural fiber clothing (cotton, wool, etc.), Bring a snack and water for break time, Price: $75 class fee + $30 materials

title: Rockin' the Gateway presents "Hipper Than Hip"
description: On August 29th it is time to get funky with the hottest horn line this side of Oakland! Hipper than Hip was formed in 2015 with the goal of bringing back the classic sounds of great horn line bands. We drew inspiration mostly from Tower of Power and then added Chicago, Earth Wind and Fire, Aretha, Tina, Stevie, Bruno, and more. If they had a great horn line, and our fans would love it, we wanted to play their music.

title: Rosangela Silvestre: 2 DANCE classes - Silvestre Technique and Orixas!

Afro-Brazilian style, inspired by Candomblé Orixá symbology, the dance integrates the four elements: Earth, Air, Water, Fire, while catalyzing an experience of heightened consciousness and personal empowerment. We may be responding to an interior message, or vibrantly expressing the fire energy of Xango! Live drumming! https://www.instagram.com/silvestreassociacaocultural/, 2 nights of DANCE classes- Sept 1 & 2, 5 -7 pm

description: Come enjoy the last bits of Summer at the beautiful North Star House. Attendees will get a tour of the iconic Julia Morgan building, including the unfinished upstairs, along with updates on upcoming events and ways to get involved with our creative community., North Star House will share about their Creative Exchange program and is seeking input from the community about what they want to see in the newly renovated 2nd floor., Our meetups are for everyone, join us!

title: AKI KUMAR & MANIC MOJO at the Wild Eye Pub
description: On Saturday, Sept 5th from 6:30 - 9:30pm the Wild Eye Pub in Grass Valley invites music lovers to their creekside stage for a live performance featuring AKI KUMAR & MANIC MOJO!, The show opens at 6:30pm with MANIC MOJO - an exciting new all originals band emerging in the Nevada County music scene! MANIC MOJO is born of the raw talent and musical synergy of its two core members, Manny Servantes and Nico Paoletti, both born and raised in Nevada County, whose shared passion for creating original music is the driving force of their unique, one of a kind sound. They are multi instrumentalist, singer songwriters and arrangers, blending influences of blues, soul, jazz, funk and rock through powerful, dynamic instrumentation and vocals. MANIC MOJO features Manny Servantes on harmonica, Nico Paoletti on guitar and vocals, Gregory S. Young on keys, Will Madrid on Bass and David Clouse on drums. Their line up of unforgettable original songs combines energetic hooks, licks and lyrics with irresistible dance grooves for a sound that is truly their own., Headlining for this event is Bay Area harmonica player and vocalist, AKI KUMAR, an Indian-born musician known for his eclectic sound, blending a deep love for American, Chicago style blues with classical melodies from his Indian heritage. A masterful harmonica player, soulful vocalist, band-leader, drummer and producer, Kumar is a man of many talents who's become well known as a prolific artist of the Sa Francisco Bay Area. His blending of retro Indian music into his presentations makes for a unique, electrifying, multi-cultural mash-up with a sound like no one else, yet his music never loses touch with the inspirational foundation it draws from the blues.

title: Omari Tau & Friends: A Portrait of America in Song
description: Baritone Omari Tau performs a genre-spanning (jazzy classical) program that is quintessentially American — spanning Kurt Weill, Fats Waller and George Gershwin, alongside new American composers and selections from Tau's own new album, Safe Thus Far. He is joined by pianist Graham Sobelman, a Sacramento-based music director whose credits include Broadway Sacramento and B Street Theatre, and cellist Natalie Hagwood of the genre-crossing ensemble Solabel., Tau is a longtime presence in the Music in the Mountains community. He has performed with the organization's community engagement programs and holiday concerts, and served as co-founding artistic director of MIM favorite Rogue Music Project. He is also a Lion King alum and Professor of Vocal Music at Cosumnes River College., Presented by Music in the Mountains, bringing world-class classical music to Nevada County since 1982. Tickets and details at musicinthemountains.org.

title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari with Live Score by the Invincible Czars
description: 9/6 - The Onyx Downtown and The Nevada City Film Festival are excited to announce the newest collaborative screening with legendary rock band The Invincible Czars, as they perform live musical accompaniment for THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI! The world’s first feature-length horror film THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI tells the story of a group of friends who encounter the mysterious doctor and his scary, sleepwalking sidekick Cesare at a carnival. When a series of murders brings the town to its knees, Franzis sets out to prove Caligari is responsible… but is he? The Invincible Czars perform their nightmarish-ly fun soundtrack along with the film as an immersive live experience, transporting audiences back 100+ years via an age-old tale accompanied by a chilling, tastefully-modern score featuring an impressive blend of traditional acoustic and present-day electric instruments. From delicate passages of longing and love to menacing motifs of dissonant horror and pain, each instrument plays a critical role establishing character themes and creating an aural dreamscape for the film. TICKETS ON SALE NOW! $20 in advance, $25 at the door.

title: Intro to Stained Glass – Level 1
description: Experience the art of stained glass in this beginner-friendly workshop! Join us to craft a small suncatcher using vibrant glass pieces in this class with Charne Morris. No experience necessary—just bring your enthusiasm!, This introductory class focuses on straight cuts and will teach you the basics of stained glass safety., Throughout this 3-hour class, you will learn pattern transfer, glass cutting, grinding, foiling, soldering, and polishing. You will go home with a finished project piece that is roughly 3.5” x 4”., A materials cost of $20 is required on the day. Payment to the facilitator can be made using cash or Venmo., What You’ll Learn:Basics of stained glass art, How glass behaves and the creation process, Selecting and cutting glass pieces, Creating a stained glass suncatcher using the copper foil method and soldering techniques, Details:Duration: 3 hours, Price: $79 class fee + plus additional material fee $20 is required during class. Payment to the facilitator can be made using cash or Venmo., Ages: Adults and 16+, What to wear: Important: Please wear long pants and close-toe shoes, Participants: Minimum of 3, maximum of 6 (Class will be rescheduled if minimum attendance is not met) Please note: All classes require a minimum number of participants and may be rescheduled if that minimum is not met. If this happens, we’ll let you know in advance and work with you to get you into the next available class., Join us for this creative journey and leave with your own stunning stained glass suncatcher!

title: Watercolor Exploration with Chappy Valente
description: Immerse yourself in the expressive world of watercolor painting! Whether you’re brand new to watercolor or looking to expand your skills, this hands-on class with artist and educator Chappy Valente will help you gain confidence and technique. Learn to paint with fluidity and intention as you explore the tools, papers, and brushwork that make watercolor such a luminous and rewarding medium., Each session is a stand-alone class with fresh projects and techniques—join once or come monthly to continue growing your watercolor practice., What’s the Project:, Create your own watercolor studies exploring washes, color mixing, and texture effects. Each class introduces a new focus—such as landscapes, botanicals, or abstract forms—to inspire your creativity., What Will They Learn:Brush control and paint-to-water ratios, Wash techniques (wet-on-wet, wet-on-dry, gradient), Paper types, brush styles, and pigment selection, Layering, and color blending, Tips for composition and adding expressive detail, Materials Needed:, All materials are provided for in-class use. Students are welcome to bring their own favorite brushes or watercolor set if desired., Skill Level / Prerequisites:, All skill levels welcome—from first-time painters to those continuing their watercolor journey., Class Length:, One 3-hour session, (Optional continuing classes offered monthly), Fee: $50 + $20 materials, Minimum 3 / Maximum 5 participants

title: Woodturning 101 – Craft a Beautiful Wooden Bowl
description: Discover the art of woodturning and learn to make a beautiful wood bowl using a wood lathe – no experience is required!, Are you interested in woodturning and looking to learn a new skill? In this class, you’ll learn how to turn a beautiful bowl out of wood using a lathe. The process is both rewarding and relaxing, as you take a piece of raw wood and turn it into a functional work of wood art. Under the guidance of our experienced instructor, you’ll start by learning the basics of wood lathe operation and safety. Once you’re comfortable with the equipment, we’ll move on to selecting and preparing the wood for turning. With the wood secured on the lathe, you’ll use a series of specially designed tools to shape the bowl. , At the end of the class, you’ll take home a beautiful, hand-turned bowl that you can be proud of. You’ll also have the woodturning skills and knowledge to continue turning bowls on your own. , Price: $160 + $40 materials, Limited spaces available. Sign up today! Class 2 minimum/3 maximum participants – (please note: if attendance does not meet minimum, class will be rescheduled) , Tools provided. If you have tools, please feel free to bring them.

title: Make a Tiny Grief Book
description: Make a Tiny Grief Book – A Book Arts Workshop, In this hands-on workshop, participants will learn to bind little “grief books,” pocket-sized tomes containing text adapted (with acknowledgment) from How to Go On Living When Someone You Love Dies by Therese Rando (Bantam Books, 1991), and beautiful original art created and donated specifically for the books by local watercolorist Maggie Orion. To see examples of finished books, visit the Grief Book Project’s website. No previous bookbinding experience is needed, and all materials are prepared and provided for you., This is part of a larger community mutual aid practice; participants have the option to keep all the books they make, or to donate one or more to local grief counseling efforts., What You’ll Learn:The anatomy of a book and how to create case-bound covers, applicable to any homemade journal project, Bookbinding Basics: How to fold, kettle stitch, and assemble a small hard-cover book using simple tools., What You’ll Create:At least one little grief book, 2.6″ x 2″, with the option to make more in the extra time, A new connection to a local network of makers who hand-bind grief books on an ongoing basis., Class Details:Ages: Adults & teens 13+, Skill Level: Beginner-friendly—no prior bookbinding experience required!, Fee: $70, Class Size: Minimum 3 / Maximum 4 participants

title: Tuesday Morning Ceramics – Hand-Building Techniques
description: Tuesday Morning Ceramics and Pottery Class with Pamela Montalbano, 6 class series, Tuesday Mornings 10:30 am – 12:30 pm, Price: $271 Public ($216 for 6 classes + $55 materials), Discover your creativity, engage your mind, and come play with clay! In this Ceramics and Pottery Class, we will use hand-building techniques to make functional and non-functional ceramics and pottery projects using slabs and coils. Clay, Glazing, and firings are included in the materials fee. Participants can sign up for additional Tuesday Morning classes each month if they wish to continue their ceramics adventure., We will be hand-building and then every third class will be a glazing class. At least 2 projects will be made in this series., Class 5 minimum/8 maximum participants – (please note: if attendance does not meet the minimum, the class will be rescheduled)

title: Make a Ceramic Witches Hat Luminary
description: In this two-day workshop, you will form a slab of clay into a cone form and complete it with decoration and holes for the light of a tea candle to shine and twinkle through. Learn fun hand-building techniques, decorate your ceramic luminary with stamps and imprints, holes and balls! Let your imagination soar. In the second class we will glaze with beautiful colors, then your luminary will be kiln-fired and ready for pick up in about one week.
